sheets.title: Python Basics
sheets.summary: Variables, data types, input and output — the everyday essentials.

sections.heading: Variables
sections.body: A variable stores a value under a name. No declaration keyword needed — just assign with =. Names are case-sensitive and use snake_case by convention.
sections.code:
age = 16
name = "Kerr"
is_student = True
print(name, age, is_student)

sections.heading: Core Data Types
sections.body: int (whole numbers), float (decimals), str (text in quotes), bool (True/False), and None (no value). Use type(x) to check, int() / float() / str() to convert.
sections.code:
x = 10        # int
y = 3.14      # float
text = "hi"   # str
flag = False  # bool

print(type(y))          # <class 'float'>
num = int("42") + 1     # convert str -> int -> 43

sections.heading: Arithmetic Operators
sections.body: + - * / as usual. Special ones: // floor division, % remainder, ** power.
sections.code:
print(7 / 2)    # 3.5  (true division)
print(7 // 2)   # 3    (floor division)
print(7 % 2)    # 1    (remainder)
print(2 ** 10)  # 1024 (power)

sections.heading: Input and Output
sections.body: input() always returns a string — convert it if you need a number. print() can take several values separated by commas.
sections.code:
name = input("Your name: ")
age = int(input("Your age: "))
print("Hello", name, "— next year you'll be", age + 1)

sections.heading: String Basics
sections.body: Strings are sequences of characters. Concatenate with +, repeat with *, get length with len(), access single characters with [index] starting at 0.
sections.code:
s = "Python"
print(len(s))     # 6
print(s[0])       # 'P'
print(s * 2)      # PythonPython
print("Py" + "!") # Py!

sheets.title: If-Else Statements
sheets.summary: Making decisions: if, elif, else, and comparison operators.

sections.heading: Comparison Operators
sections.body: == equal, != not equal, < less, > greater, <= and >=. Note: = assigns, == compares. Chained comparisons work: 0 <= x <= 100.
sections.code:
score = 85
print(score == 100)   # False
print(score >= 75)    # True

sections.heading: if / elif / else
sections.body: Only the first true branch runs. Indentation (4 spaces) defines the block — this is required syntax in Python, not style.

sections.heading: Logical Operators
sections.body: Combine conditions with and (both must be true), or (at least one), not (flips).

sections.heading: Truthiness
sections.body: Empty values count as False: 0, "", [], {}, None. Everything else is True — so `if my_list:` means "if the list has items".

sheets.title: Loops
sheets.summary: for loops, while loops, range(), break and continue.

sections.heading: for Loops and range()
sections.body: Loop over a sequence. range(n) counts 0..n-1; range(start, stop, step) for custom ranges.

sections.heading: while Loops
sections.body: Repeats while the condition stays True. Always change something inside the loop or it runs forever.
sections.code:
count = 3
while count > 0:
    print(count)
    count -= 1     # countdown: 3 2 1
print("Lift off!")

sections.heading: break and continue
sections.body: break exits the loop immediately; continue skips to the next iteration.

sections.heading: Nested Loops
sections.body: A loop inside a loop — the inner one completes fully for every outer step.

sheets.title: Functions
sheets.summary: Defining functions, parameters, return values, and scope.

sections.heading: Defining and Calling
sections.body: def name(parameters): creates a function; call it with name(arguments). The body runs only when called.

sections.heading: Parameters & Arguments
sections.body: Parameters are placeholders; arguments are the real values. You can give defaults, and pass keyword arguments out of order.
sections.code:
def intro(name, greeting="Hi"):
    print(f"{greeting}, {name}!")

intro("Ana")                    # Hi, Ana!
intro("Ben", greeting="Welcome")  # Welcome, Ben!

sections.heading: Return Values
sections.body: return sends a result back to the caller and ends the function. A function with no return gives back None.
sections.code:
def area(w, h):
    return w * h

a = area(3, 4)
print(a)          # 12

sections.heading: Scope
sections.body: Variables created inside a function are local — they disappear after it ends. Functions read outer variables but shouldn't modify them without global (avoid that).
sections.code:
total = 0

def add(points):
    local = points * 2   # local only
    return local

print(add(5))   # 10
# print(local)  # NameError — doesn't exist here

sections.heading: Docstrings
sections.body: A triple-quoted string on the first line documents what the function does. Read it with help(func).

sheets.title: Lists, Tuples, Sets & Dictionaries
sheets.summary: Python's built-in collections and when to use each.

sections.heading: Lists
sections.body: Ordered, changeable collections. Index from 0, slice with [start:stop], append/remove/insert to modify.
sections.code:
scores = [90, 85, 77]
scores.append(100)
scores[0] = 95
print(scores[:2])   # first two: [95, 85]
print(len(scores))  # 4

sections.heading: Useful List Methods
sections.body: append(x) adds to end, insert(i, x), remove(x) deletes by value, sort() orders in place, sum()/max()/min() reduce.
sections.code:
nums = [3, 1, 4]
nums.sort()
print(nums)          # [1, 3, 4]
nums.remove(3)
print(sum(nums))     # 5

sections.heading: List Comprehensions
sections.body: Build a list in one line: [expression for item in sequence if condition].
sections.code:
squares = [n**2 for n in range(5)]
print(squares)               # [0, 1, 4, 9, 16]
evens = [n for n in squares if n % 2 == 0]
print(evens)                 # [0, 4, 16]

sections.heading: Tuples
sections.body: Like lists but immutable — cannot be changed after creation. Use for fixed groups of values.
sections.code:
point = (3, 4)
x, y = point       # unpacking
print(x + y)       # 7
# point[0] = 9     # TypeError!

sections.heading: Sets
sections.body: Unordered collection with NO duplicates — great for deduplicating and membership tests.
sections.code:
tags = ["py", "web", "py"]
unique = set(tags)
print(unique)         # {'py', 'web'}
print("py" in unique) # True (fast lookup)

sections.heading: Dictionaries
sections.body: Key → value pairs. Access by key, .get() won't crash on missing keys, loop over .items().

sheets.title: Modules & Imports
sheets.summary: Using the standard library and organizing code into modules.

sections.heading: Importing Modules
sections.body: import module uses dot notation; from module import name imports directly; import x as y renames.
sections.code:
import math
print(math.sqrt(16))    # 4.0

from random import randint
print(randint(1, 6))    # dice roll

import datetime as dt
print(dt.date.today())

sections.heading: Handy Standard Library
sections.body: math (numbers), random (chance), datetime (dates/times), os (files/system), json (data files). These ship with Python — nothing to install.
sections.code:
from math import pi, ceil
print(pi)          # 3.14159...
print(ceil(2.1))   # 3

sections.heading: Creating Your Own Module
sections.body: Any .py file is a module. Import your own file by its name (must be in the same folder). Code under `if __name__ == "__main__":` runs only when the file itself is run, not when imported.

sheets.title: Output Formatting, Files & JSON
sheets.summary: f-strings, alignment, reading/writing files, saving data as JSON.

sections.heading: f-Strings
sections.body: Put f before the quotes and drop variables or expressions right inside {}.
sections.code:
name = "Ana"
score = 91.567
print(f"{name} scored {score:.1f}%")  # Ana scored 91.6%
print(f"{score=}")                    # score=91.567 (debug form)

sections.heading: Alignment and Padding
sections.body: Inside f-string braces: :>N right-align, :<N left-align, :^N center, :.Nf decimal places.

sections.heading: Reading & Writing Files
sections.body: with open(...) as f handles closing automatically. Modes: "w" write (overwrites!), "a" append, "r" read.
sections.code:
with open("notes.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write("Line one\n")

with open("notes.txt", "r") as f:
    for line in f:
        print(line.strip())

sections.heading: JSON — Saving Structured Data
sections.body: json.dumps/loads convert between Python objects and JSON strings; json.dump/load do it straight to/from files.
sections.code:
import json

progress = {"completed": ["lesson-1-1"], "streak": 3}

with open("save.json", "w") as f:
    json.dump(progress, f)

with open("save.json") as f:
    loaded = json.load(f)
print(loaded["streak"])   # 3

sheets.title: Errors & Exceptions
sheets.summary: Why programs crash, try/except, raising errors, and finally.

sections.heading: Common Exceptions
sections.body: SyntaxError — code isn't valid Python. Others happen at runtime: ValueError (right type, bad value), TypeError (wrong type), ZeroDivisionError, IndexError, KeyError, FileNotFoundError.
sections.code:
# int("abc")      -> ValueError
# 10 / 0           -> ZeroDivisionError
# [1,2][5]         -> IndexError
# d["missing"]     -> KeyError

sections.heading: try / except
sections.body: Wrap risky code in try; the except block runs only if that specific error happens. Catch specific types — bare except hides real bugs.

sections.heading: Multiple except Blocks & else
sections.body: Different errors, different handling. else runs when no error happened.

sections.heading: raise and finally
sections.body: raise creates an error deliberately with a message. finally runs no matter what — good for clean-up.

sheets.title: Classes & OOP (+ Generators)
sheets.summary: Classes, objects, inheritance, iterators and generators.

sections.heading: Class Basics
sections.body: A class is a blueprint; each object made from it is an instance. __init__ sets up new instances; self refers to the current one.

sections.heading: Inheritance
sections.body: A child class reuses and extends a parent class. Call super().__init__() to run the parent's setup.

sections.heading: Iterators & Generators
sections.body: Generators produce values one at a time with yield — memory-friendly for big sequences. Each next() resumes where it left off.

An error detected during execution that can be caught with try/except.
A number with a decimal point, e.g. 3.14.
A named, reusable block of code defined with def.
The position of an item in a sequence; counting starts at 0.
A whole number, e.g. 42.
The program that reads and executes Python code line by line.
Anything you can loop over with for: lists, strings, ranges, generators.
A text format for structured data; Python converts to/from it with the json module.
An ordered, changeable collection written with square brackets [ ].
Code that repeats — with for (known count/sequence) or while (condition).
A file of reusable Python code that you can import.
A single instance of a class, holding its own data.
The placeholder variable in a function definition.
Sends a value back from a function to wherever it was called.
An unordered collection with no duplicate items.
Text, written inside quotes: "hello".
An ordered collection that cannot be changed after creation, written ( ).
A named container for a value, created by assignment (=).
